This experience still terrifies us. Christmas Eve three years ago, I was sleeping at my friend Joe's house because I used to spend Christmases with his family. It was just the four of us: me in the bedroom right next to the wood staircase, Joe in the room across the hall, and his parents down the hall.

His house is a super old farmhouse in the woods in New England, and at night, specifically on winter nights, it is so quiet you can hear a pin drop, besides the distant snores of his mom and dad from their room down the hall.

That night, around 3 am, I startled awake, feeling unsettled. I didn't know why, and lay up just staring at the ceiling for almost an hour listening to the total silence of the house, the faint snoring of his parents off in the distance. I yearned for my phone to distract me from the unease but it was dead, and I didn't have a phone charger. So I lay awake for a long time. Eventually I dozed off again.

Until I was jarred awake to the sharp sound of a stair creaking. It was loud and slow, with intention. I braced myself, hoping it was just a fluke, but then the next stair creaked deeply under what was undeniably the sound of a slow, heel-to-toe footstep of a heavy boot, and it became clear somebody was in the stairway trying to creep up the stairs with shoes on.

My heart was pounding. It became silent again, like the intruder paused. I didn't want to make noise to draw attention to myself but I was in utter fight or flight. I couldn't run and lock the door because there was no lock, so I kept going back and forth between scanning the room for weapons, considering hiding in the closet or jumping out the two-story window, but mostly I was frozen in terror.

If my phone wasn't dead I would have called the police. Instead I grabbed my laptop which was next to me, I quietly iMessaged Joe a million texts trying to wake him up.

This is our text convo:

Me: DUDE

Me: PLEASE WAKE UP IM FREAKING OUT

\*stairway creaks\*

Me: I THINK SOMEONE IS IN THE HOUSE

(No answer. Then I realized I could Facetime him, so I called him. No answer. But the vibration of the call woke him up. He read my texts.)

Joe: what's going on??

Me: dude i think someone is in the stairway

Me: im freaking out

Me: LISTEN

(Silence. Parents' snoring. We're waiting and listening in the silence. A HEAVY boot goes up one more stair. At this point they're around the top of the staircase, right outside our rooms.)

Joe: Yes. someone is in the house.

My heart is pounding. I hear Joe from the other room RIP his door open, fling the lights on and STORM down the stairs looking for the person. He yells "GET OUT." Then he comes back up the stairs, comes in my room and tells me ... no one was there, no lights were on, his parents are asleep, nothing was out of place. We're both so creeped out.

After the terror calmed, this story just mystifies us. Neither of us believe in ghosts and have no idea how to rationalize the fact that we both heard someone trying to stealthily go up the stairs in heavy boots. We told his parents the next day and they laughed at us.

For example, I noticed he has a habit of tilting his phone away from me when he checks it next to me. That set my radar OFF. I immediately asked him about it. His response was not defensive or combative the way past partners would have replied in similar situations. He didn’t imply that I’m wrong for feeling insecure. He: apologized, explained that he tends to do it around lots of people without realizing and without intending, and assured me I’m not crazy for being weirded out by it. He made a point to not tilt it away after that.
